text: In FACS-based directed evolution screening, a researcher typically gates on approximately what fraction of cells to enrich for the desired fluorescent phenotype?
choices: Exactly the single brightest cell in the population
explanation: Standard FACS-based enrichment gates on the top 0.1-1% of fluorescent cells, often across multiple rounds of sorting, to enrich for rare improved variants within a large library while retaining enough diversity to find true positives. Gating on 25-50% would be far too permissive to enrich rare variants, isolating a single cell is not how population-level sorting works in practice, and gating on the least fluorescent cells would select against, rather than for, the desired activity in a standard positive screen.
